`scripts/field_study.py` answered "what do the profitable teams do differently, in ratios".

A Charge is recovered from `amount`, and `amount` on an accepted row is `min(a, c)`, not `a`.

**2,933.51 (G28 #7) and 4,649.21 (G29 #2), both paid 2,000.00**. So those "2,000.00 Charges"
are truncations of unknown larger Charges, and every team that looks like it anchored on 2,000
merely charged *something above it*. Once cap-censored rows are removed, exact-round Charges
above 500 number **0 for eyay, error404 ai, TakeTheMoneyAndRun, OPUSMOPUS and Codacabana**.
See `cap_report()` and `anchor_report()`.

The Cap model that survives all settled Games (`--cap`):

    c = max(4t, 2000)

* **Floor.** Items with `t < 60` and `t < 246` paid out exactly `2,000.00`, which cannot be
  `4t`. Our own 4,649.21 was truncated to 2,000.00, so `c = 2000` *exactly* there -- not
  merely `>= 2000`.
* **Slope.** Ties at *non-round* values pin `4t`: G19 #4 four issuers at `3,848.48`
  (`/4 = 962.12`, inside the bracket `[854.5, 1242.0)`) and G27 #3 three issuers at
  `12,000.00` (`/4 = 3000.00`, inside `[3000.0, 3022.2)`). A tie to the cent at a non-round
  number is not independent estimation.
* **No counterexample.** No accepted row with a bounded `t` exceeds `max(4*t_hi, 2000)`.

Two consequences that matter more than the Cap itself:

1. **Any Charge above `max(4t̂, 2000)` is strictly wasteful** (R5/R6c): it cannot increase what
   a reviewer pays and can only reduce who accepts.
2. **Reconstruction is contaminated on cap-censored items.** A Charge recovered only from
   accepted rows at `>= 2000` is a *lower bound*, and a rejection of such an issuer yields a
   *wrong* `b_hi` for the reviewer. `charge_status()` labels every recovered Charge so the
   contaminated ones can be excluded rather than quietly believed.

"""Replay a Game with a hypothetical submission of ours, against the real Field.

What this is for
----------------
The published Transactions of a settled Game contain, for every ordered pair of teams and
every Line Item, whether the Charge was accepted and how much money moved. That is enough
to reconstruct *everybody else's behaviour* and to bracket the secret Fair Value `t`. Once
we have those, we can ask the counterfactual that actually matters:

    what would our net have been in Game g if we had submitted (a, b) instead?

holding every opponent's real Charge and Limit fixed. That turns tuning -- of the Fair

instead of an argument.

**Nothing broke, and that is the first result.** The degradation path held exactly as designed:
the blind floor posted at T+0, Price Memory priced what it recognised, the fitted constants
covered the rest, and eight Games banked **+254,092 weighted**. Rule 1 says the default submission

the model is real rather than aspirational.

**The tempting conclusion is that the model channel is dead weight, and it does not survive a
test.** Normalising by the oracle ceiling, because Case value swings twentyfold and raw per-Game
nets cannot be compared:

| | n | mean capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: |

A +10.8 point gap. But capture has a standard deviation of 34 % dark and **75 %** live, ranging
from −296 % to +434 %, and a permutation test over 200,000 shuffles gives **p = 0.208**. One split
in five is this lopsided by chance. Not actionable.

**What the estimates say, with an honest caveat.** Bucketed on `t̂` — the only split knowable at
submission time — every bucket estimates *high*: 2.36x under 100, 1.87x at 100-400, 1.73x at

stage fires only when `t̂ < t_lo`, so **it selects the left tail by construction**, and acting on it

Done. Here's where it landed.

## Timing reality first

Game 98 submitted cleanly a few minutes ago. **Only Games 99 (11:37) and 100 (11:50) remain**, deadline 12:00. The runner is healthy and armed. That constraint shaped everything below.

## Where we actually stand

We are **"Bin busy", 5th of 17** at 260,250 — but that number hides the story:

| | all-time | last 20 Games | first 80 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Codacabana | 848,081 | 654,377 | 193,704 |
| eyay | 710,048 | 426,763 | 283,285 |
| error404 ai | 476,491 | 149,110 | 327,382 |
| TakeTheMoneyAndRun | 444,812 | 469,135 | −24,323 |
| **Bin busy** | **260,250** | **332,001** | **−71,752** |

In the triple-weighted final stretch we are **4th, ahead of error404 ai by 2.2×**. Our all-time rank is a debt from the first 80 Games, not current form.

## The finding

I bucketed our own rejections by how far each opponent's Charge sat above **our own Limit**. The payoff table makes this a single threshold — reject costs `1.5a` if the claim was fair, `0` if not; accept costs `a` — so **accept iff `q = P(fair) > 2/3`**:

| `a / b` | n | `q` | gain from accepting |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **1.00–1.25×** | 412 | **83 %** | **+33,898** |
| 1.25–1.50× | 145 | 54 % | −6,444 |
| 1.50–2.00× | 134 | 44 % | −12,497 |
| 2.00–3.00× | 145 | 32 % | −25,767 |
| > 3× | 244 | 25 % | −73,441 |

`q` falls monotonically — **the Limit ranks claims correctly, it just sits ~25 % too low.** Every band above 1.25× is already on the right side. We are not too strict in general; we are too strict in exactly one narrow band, worth **≈ +102k weighted** over Games 82–97 (~6.4k/Game).

The field corroborates it, same Games and same Cases: we accept **44 %** (lowest of any scoring team) yet pay the **highest** total Reviewer cost — 324,812 against Codacabana's 265,624, of which penalties are **80 % of our costs against their 26 %**. Our income (378,386) is within 11 % of theirs, so **57 % of the gap to first is Reviewer-side.**

The censoring cuts our way for once: the 217 unrecoverable rejections are ones all sixteen reviewers rejected at zero — the signature of large *fraudulent* Charges — so excluding them biases `q` **upward**. It breaks only if 101 of 217 land in the narrowest, lowest band, which by construction they cannot.

## What I did and didn't do

Held the pipeline, as you chose — max capture was ~12.7k against a 185k gap to 4th, so it couldn't move the standing, while a bad edit risked a Game worth up to 96,869. Recorded as **H20** in the hypothesis ledger with the full derivation, and added **`scripts/limit_margin.py`** so it reproduces. Nothing committed.

**One thing to flag for the pitch:** this contradicts a line in CLAUDE.md — *"a high `b` buys no protection from the lawyer at all, it only converts zeros into payments."* That's wrong as stated. Raising `b` converts a `1.5a` penalty into an `a` payment on every *fair* claim it newly admits, saving `0.5a`; it only converts zeros into payments on fraudulent ones. Which dominates is exactly the `q > 2/3` test. I left the correction in H20 rather than editing CLAUDE.md, since someone is editing the repo concurrently right now.

That correction is probably your strongest pitch material: a documented belief, falsified by measurement on settled data, with the euro figure attached and the reason it wasn't shipped.
